basis: Mitochondrial energy-metabolism disorder; neurologic dysfunction and myopathy commonly exceed ~30%; other organ damage varies substantially by subtype.
Brachial plexus compression defines neurogenic TOS; rib anomalies predispose to compression, while pain alone does not establish musculoskeletal damage.
Disorder of triglyceride-rich lipoprotein metabolism; pancreatitis and atherosclerotic disease are separately diagnosed complications.
Reported family has myopathy/joint disease, skin fragility and retinal degeneration; malabsorption is a defining feature. Hypothyroidism omitted at cap; nephroptosis alone is not renal damage.
Immune-mediated lichen planopilaris variant causing scarring scalp alopecia and follicular skin disease.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with developmental delay in 6/7; ptosis in 2/7 is borderline, with other ocular and renal abnormalities individually only 1/7.
Carcinoma arising in urinary tract urothelium, including bladder, ureter, urethra and renal pelvis.
Hemolysis, thrombocytopenia and microvascular thrombosis define TTP; most cases are autoimmune. CNS ischemic dysfunction occurs in 30-79%; renal impairment is only 5-29%.
Localized necrosis of breast adipose tissue; breast disease has no axis.
Mesenchymal soft-tissue neoplasm with pericytic differentiation; assigned to the musculoskeletal soft-tissue axis.
Adenocarcinoma arising in the ethmoid sinus; paranasal sinuses belong to the pulmonary axis.
Hypospadias and urogenital sinus anomalies are reported in 80-99% and affect urethral anatomy; gonadal/genital differentiation otherwise falls outside the axes.
Persistent disease of multiple peripheral nerves; the umbrella does not imply a specific immune or metabolic cause.
Multiple skeletal joint fusions define the syndrome; conductive hearing impairment from ossicular fixation occurs in 80-99%.
Neurologic movement disorder defined by persistent motor or vocal tics.
Skeletal thoracic dysplasia with characteristic pulmonary hypoplasia/asphyxia; cerebellar malformation and tongue hamartoma each reported in 1/2. Renal frequency unspecified.
Localized dermal elastic-tissue disorder causing persistent skin laxity and impaired recoil; hyperesthesia alone does not establish nerve damage.
Squamous carcinoma confined to the skin epidermis.
Combined immunodeficiency defined by absent T and B lymphocytes; neurologic, visual and hearing abnormalities are only occasional (5-29%).
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy causing recurrent seizures and cognitive and motor impairment.
Osteosclerosis and brain abnormalities define Raine syndrome; pulmonary hypoplasia occurs in 4/7, cleft palate in 80-99%, and gingival fibromatosis in 30-79%.
Localized cutaneous mucin deposition; gammopathy and systemic manifestations are alternative presentations without evidence that any additional organ is damaged in >=30%.
Benign tumour occupying the nasal cavity, which belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Neutral lipid storage disorder with pathological triglyceride deposition in myocardium and coronary vasculature.
Severe recessive protein S deficiency commonly causes necrotic neonatal purpura fulminans; cerebral hemorrhage/seizures reported in 1/1. Ocular damage frequency unspecified.
